description: Vietnamese press reporting in 2025 credits this airframe with 13 aircraft destroyed and associates it with ace Nguyen Van Coc. Displayed outdoors in the museum yard off Thang Long street beside Tan Son Nhat airport.

The A-37 flown by Tu De of the Quyet Thang (Determined to Win) squadron which dropped the first bombs on Tan Son Nhat air base on 28 April 1975, using captured VNAF aircraft. Note that the Air Defence-Air Force Museum in Hanoi also states it holds an A-37 from this action.

Ex-VNAF fighter-bomber; museum text credits it with over 1000 sorties and 2026 bombs dropped after capture. Compiled listings call it an F-5A. The Air Force Museum in Hanoi displays an F-5 photographed in April 2025 also wearing 7579, so one of the two carries the other's number; the Ho Chi Minh City number is recorded here because it is corroborated by two 2025 Vietnamese press reports with photographs.
Ex-VNAF Huey captured in 1975 and used post-war by the VPAF.
VPAF transport helicopter displayed in the museum yard.
VPAF attack helicopter; museum text records 94 combat sorties between 1984 and 1986. Distinct from Mi-24A 7430 at the Air Force Museum in Hanoi.
Ex-VNAF liaison aircraft. Compiled listings give the number 764, but the Air Force Museum in Hanoi displays a U-17 photographed in April 2025 also wearing 764, so tail_number is left blank.
MiG-17 listed among the museum's aircraft in 2025 Vietnamese press coverage; no number given.
